title: Earl Hines, Joe Glaser and choosing New York over Chicago
summary: Hines heard Hawkins at 'Bama State and told Joe Glaser, who offered a ticket; on his aunt's advice Hawkins went to New York and got a break at the Harlem Opera House.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You mentioned before that Earl Hines had told Joe Glaser something about you?

Right. I, oh yeah. I was in 'Bama State then. Earl Hines came down with his band to play a concert on the campus and I was in school then. And, we each would alternate. We did that with all the bands that came there.
So, when Earl got back to Chicago,

Earl told Joe Glaser about me. That, of course, is just like I said. I just, high notes than (inaudible) to me were nothing. I mean, cause I was used to it. You know? I was hitting the C on account of, well, Foster. I used to try and copy everything he did, go through like he would hit that al-tissimo high C then. And then, I just started to try and keep up with him. You know?

And then, I told Joe Glaser about him a month later. Joe sent a letter and a ticket, and also, oh, let me see, about $100 for a little money. But, I kept that month, and I thought it over (inaudible). My aunt told me, she was living in New Jersey, in Newark. I told her I was going to Chicago. I had an opportunity to go to Chicago. So, thought it out. She said you'd better stay there cause she was, and if you're going away, you'd better come to New York. So, in case things don't work out for you, I can kinda help look out for you. So, I got back in touch with Joe Glaser, thanked him very much, and Joe told me,
said if anytime you want me or need me in New York or anywhere, just let me know. It was very nice of him. He and I were still friends up until the time he passed.
And so, I went to New York with the band. Then, I got a break at the Harlem Opera House.

So, we went in there, and had never played a stage show before. We had Jackie "Moms" Mabley, the Steppe Brothers. We don't know nothing about show music, but we, they taught us. And, Christina Banks and the chorus line.
I'd like to stay before 'Bama State, you know, for a little while. We're gonna get right to that a little later.
